declaration_note: Committed in its own commit before the probe was extended or re-run. outcomes.declared.json is left byte-identical, INCLUDING the mislabelled O6 — the erratum below corrects the record without rewriting a pre-declaration after seeing its result.

errata_against_cycle_1.cycle_1_label: a competing page-level document rule `img { object-fit: contain }` of equal specificity present
errata_against_cycle_1.correction: "of equal specificity" was written against `::slotted(img)` and is loose even there (`::slotted(img)` is (0,0,2); a bare `img` is (0,0,1)). Against the side that matters — the STATIC rewrite `.sk-entity-marker__content > img` at (0,1,1) — the bare `img` rule plainly LOSES. O5's measured result is unaffected and its conclusion stands; only the label was wrong. Cycle-1 review did not catch this one; it is corrected here for the same reason O6 is.
errata_against_cycle_1.what_the_new_outcomes_do: The three regimes are named explicitly in `competing_rule_regimes` below, so no outcome in this construct kind describes a specificity relationship without stating both sides of it.

errata_against_cycle_1.cycle_1_label: the same competing rule at HIGHER specificity `.page-scope img { object-fit: contain }`
errata_against_cycle_1.correction: `.page-scope img` is (0,1,1). The library's static rewrite `.sk-entity-marker__content > img` is ALSO (0,1,1). They TIE; the consumer does not outbid. O6's cycle-1 result (both forms compute `contain`) was therefore decided by document ORDER — exemplar.html appends the consumer rule last — and not by specificity, and the cycle-1 conclusion drawn from it ("the static form yields only when the page outbids it") does not follow from it.
errata_against_cycle_1.what_the_new_outcomes_do: O7-O10 separate the three regimes the cycle-1 set conflated — consumer LOSES on specificity, consumer TIES, consumer genuinely OUTBIDS — and vary stylesheet order within each, so the tie's order-dependence is measured rather than inferred.

why_these_outcomes_exist.MEDIUM-1: #304 is told to freeze the authoring instruction this measurement produces. The cycle-1 instruction says a static consumer must 'outbid this rule on specificity' but never states where the boundary is, and scoping with one wrapper class — the most ordinary thing a consumer does — lands exactly on the tie, where behaviour depends on sheet order the consumer often does not control.

competing_rule_regimes.weak: img { object-fit: contain } — (0,0,1), loses on specificity to the static rewrite
competing_rule_regimes.tie: .page-scope img { object-fit: contain } — (0,1,1), ties the static rewrite
competing_rule_regimes.strong: .page-scope.theme img { object-fit: contain } — (0,2,1), genuinely outbids the static rewrite

pass_bar: Unchanged from cycle 1, applied to the combined set. Note the cycle-1 verdict for this construct kind is already shadow-only on O5 alone; these outcomes exist to make the SHIPPED AUTHORING INSTRUCTION correct, not to reopen the verdict.
